symptoms: Write latency spiked to 4200ms on primary-db

output.classification_reasoning: The primary symptom is a dramatic increase in write latency (4200ms) on the primary database used by the payment-processor service, indicating a performance degradation at the data storage layer. The secondary telemetry spike on the same service suggests the issue propagates upstream but originates from the database. No network errors, authentication failures, or application code exceptions are reported, and the impact is limited to write operations rather than full service outage. The latency spike likely involves query contention, lock escalation, or resource saturation, which typically requires investigation of DB metrics, query plans, and resource allocation—tasks beyond a simple fix but not requiring a full architectural redesign, placing the incident at a moderate level of operational complexity.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
output.security_notes: Verify write freeze before node reboot. Promote read-replica prior to primary teardown.

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: Historical correlation indicates recurring pattern in payment-processor.

output.justification: The incident affects 150 users, exceeding the 100‑user threshold defined for a moderate disruption. The outage duration is 30 minutes, which is within the acceptable window for Tier‑1 services before escalation to a higher severity. The diagnostic stage is "Root Cause Confirmed" with a high confidence score (0.95), confirming the impact without evidence of widespread service degradation or critical business impact. Therefore, according to the corporate SLA, the incident meets the criteria for SEV-3.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Access and Cluster Context
remediation_steps.description: Confirm that the operator has root access or the AWS SSO role ProdOperations and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster in us-east-1.
commands: aws sts get-caller-identity
kubectl config current-context
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep $(hostname)
verification: AWS identity matches ProdOperations role
kubectl context equals prod-us-east-1
Node list shows expected production node names

remediation_steps.title: Verify Write Freeze and Promote Read Replica
remediation_steps.description: Ensure a write‑freeze is in place to prevent new writes to the primary DB, then promote the healthy read‑replica to become the new primary.
commands: curl -X POST https://write-freeze.internal/activate
kubectl exec -n database primary-db-0 -- psql -c "SELECT pg_is_in_recovery();"
kubectl exec -n database replica-db-0 -- psql -c "SELECT pg_promote();"
kubectl exec -n database primary-db-0 -- psql -c "SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state='idle in transaction';"
verification: Write‑freeze endpoint returns 200 OK
Replica reports pg_is_in_recovery = false (now primary)
Old primary reports pg_is_in_recovery = true (now replica)
No new write errors observed for 2 minutes

remediation_steps.title: Graceful Reboot of Original Primary Node
remediation_steps.description: Reboot the former primary node after promotion to allow it to sync as a replica and clear any lingering latency spikes.
commands: aws ssm send-command --instance-ids i-0abcd1234efgh5678 --document-name "AWS-RunShellScript" --parameters commands=['sudo reboot']
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/<old-primary-node-name> --timeout=300s
kubectl exec -n database replica-db-0 -- psql -c "SELECT pg_last_xlog_replay_location();"
verification: Node reports Ready status within timeout
Replication lag < 500ms for 5 consecutive checks
Payment‑processor latency returns to < 200ms

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Run synthetic health checks and verify that error rates have returned to baseline for the payment‑processor service.
commands: curl -sSf https://payment-processor.internal/healthz
kubectl logs deployment/payment-processor -c app --since=5m | grep ERR_DATABASE_PROBLEM_611 || true
kubectl get hpa payment-processor -o json | jq '.status.currentMetrics'
verification: Health endpoint returns HTTP 200 with status OK
No ERR_DATABASE_PROBLEM_611 entries in logs for the last 5 minutes
HPA metrics show stable CPU/memory within target range

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: If any verification step fails, revert the database promotion and redeploy the original primary image tag, then disable the write‑freeze.

steps.description: Disable write‑freeze to allow writes to the current primary.
commands: curl -X POST https://write-freeze.internal/deactivate
verification: Write‑freeze endpoint returns 200 OK and status = inactive

steps.description: Demote the promoted replica back to read‑only and promote the original primary back to primary.
commands: kubectl exec -n database replica-db-0 -- psql -c "SELECT pg_rewind('primary-db-0');"
kubectl exec -n database primary-db-0 -- psql -c "SELECT pg_promote();"
verification: Original primary reports pg_is_in_recovery = false
Former replica reports pg_is_in_recovery = true

steps.description: Rollback payment‑processor deployment to the previous stable image tag.
commands: kubectl rollout undo deployment/payment-processor
verification: Deployment revision matches pre‑remediation tag
Pods reach READY state within 2 minutes

commands: curl -sSf https://payment-processor.internal/healthz
kubectl logs deployment/payment-processor -c app --since=5m | grep ERR_DATABASE_PROBLEM_611 || true
verification: Health endpoint returns OK
No error signatures present in logs

prerequisite_checks: Operator credentials verified (root or ProdOperations role)
Write‑freeze policy approved by change management
All commands reviewed and approved in runbook RB-114
safety_verification.notes: All steps are documented, reversible, and include verification checkpoints before proceeding to the next step.
